0-northborough-road-common-driveway.name: 0 Northborough Road common driveway special permit
0-northborough-road-common-driveway.description: Special permit application to allow 15 feet of frontage on an 8-acre parcel to divide the land into two residential building lots served by a common driveway.
0-northborough-road-common-driveway.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a frontage variance on September 16 allowing two residential building lots to use a 15-foot right-of-way across state land, while accepting the applicant's withdrawal of the companion special permit application. Town counsel clarified that the board had authority over the frontage relief but cannot create building lots. The project must now seek subdivision approval from the Planning Board before the parcel can be divided.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 16 to grant the frontage variance and 5-0 to accept the withdrawal of the special permit application.
A relative of the applicant spoke in favor, citing a previous local project permitted with access across water department property.

0-southville-road.name: 0 Southville Road apartment development
0-southville-road.description: Proposed construction of two apartment buildings and associated infrastructure at 0 Southville Road.
0-southville-road.status: The proposed construction of two apartment buildings at 0 Southville Road remains under review by the Conservation Commission. On October 8, the commission voted to continue the hearing on the Notice of Intent and stormwater management permit after the applicant requested a continuance. The applicant has been revising site plans in response to peer review feedback.

positions.detail: Has continued the Notice of Intent and stormwater permit hearing through multiple meetings, most recently on Oct 8 while the applicant addresses peer review feedback.

0-valley-road-trail.name: 0 Valley Road footbridge and trail
0-valley-road-trail.description: Proposed construction of a wooden boardwalk and trail connection on Southborough Open Land Foundation land off Valley Road.
0-valley-road-trail.status: The Conservation Commission approved an Order of Conditions on July 29, 2026, allowing an Eagle Scout project to construct a wooden boardwalk and trail connection on Southborough Open Land Foundation property at 0 Valley Road. The commission concluded that pressure-treated wood was environmentally acceptable and the work satisfied wetlands protection standards, despite abutter objections regarding street parking, privacy, and trespassing. With the statutory appeal period passed, construction may proceed under the permit's general and special conditions.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0-1 on July 29, 2026 to issue an Order of Conditions after confirming the project met wetlands standards and was exempt from water quality certification.
The Southborough Open Land Foundation supported the passive recreation trail, while Valley Road abutters raised concerns over traffic, lack of safe parking, trespassing, and wildlife impacts.

1-overlook-drive-pool.name: 1 Overlook Drive swimming pool
1-overlook-drive-pool.description: Notice of Intent to construct an inground swimming pool, patio, and cabana within the wetland buffer zone at 1 Overlook Drive.
1-overlook-drive-pool.status: The project is approved. On October 8, 2026, the Conservation Commission voted 4-0 to close the public hearing and issue an Order of Conditions for the pool, patio, and cabana. Construction is subject to conditions requiring eight native mitigation shrubs maintained in perpetuity and a pre-construction review of equipment access protections.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on October 8, 2026, to approve the Order of Conditions with conditions on machinery access and native plantings.

104-boston-road-water-appeal.name: 104 Boston Road water bill appeal
104-boston-road-water-appeal.description: Abatement appeal before the Water Commissioners regarding an underground leak and high water bill at 104 Boston Road.
104-boston-road-water-appeal.status: The appeal has been resolved following the Select Board's decision, acting as Water Commissioners, to grant a partial abatement. On September 15, the board voted 4-0-1 to reduce the $2,872.03 bill resulting from an underground leak down to $1,100, covering the town's wholesale water costs while providing relief to the property owner. No further municipal action is required.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0-1 on Sep 15 to approve a partial abatement reducing the bill to $1,100.
A resident urged the board to grant full relief citing the farm's long history in town and advocated for expedited smart meter installation.

14-newton-street.name: 14 Newton Street garage and ADU
14-newton-street.description: Notice of Intent to construct a detached garage with an accessory dwelling unit and replacement septic in the wetland buffer at 14 Newton Street.
14-newton-street.status: The proposal to construct a detached garage, accessory dwelling unit, and replacement septic system at 14 Newton Street has secured its required local approvals. The Conservation Commission issued an Order of Conditions in July 2026, and the Board of Health voted 2-1 in August 2026 to grant a setback variance for the expanded septic system despite concerns over increasing flow on a constrained lot. The applicant must install erosion controls and request an inspection before beginning construction.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0-1 on July 29, 2026, to issue an Order of Conditions after reviewing revised stormwater infiltration plans.
Voted 2-1 on Aug 11, 2026, to approve setback variances for the septic system, with the chair dissenting over granting relief for an expansion on a constrained lot.

154-turnpike-road.name: 154 Turnpike Road site plan modification
154-turnpike-road.description: Major site plan approval modification and landscaping compliance for commercial development at 154 Turnpike Road.
154-turnpike-road.status: Major site plan modifications for 154 Turnpike Road remain under review by the Planning Board to address landscaping and exterior lighting non-compliance. The applicant, Capital Group Properties, has submitted updated sign fixture details and proposed dimmer switches to meet lighting standards, subject to an evening site visit by board members. The public hearing is set to resume on October 19, 2026, when the board will consider a draft decision ahead of an extended October 23 deadline.

positions.detail: Reviewing proposed lighting dimmers and landscaping remedies for site non-compliance, with a draft decision scheduled for presentation on October 19.

154-turnpike-road.next: Planning Board continued public hearing on October 19, 2026

170-woodland-road-coc.name: 170 Woodland Road Certificate of Compliance
170-woodland-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review for pool, patio, and drainage work within wetland resource areas at 170 Woodland Road.
170-woodland-road-coc.status: The Conservation Commission approved a Certificate of Compliance for completed residential work at 170 Woodland Road on June 4, 2026. The approval followed a site inspection confirming that required mitigation plantings and trees were healthy and in good condition. The review is complete, and no further action is required.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on June 4, 2026, to issue the Certificate of Compliance after staff confirmed required mitigation plantings were healthy.

200-turnpike-road.name: 200 Turnpike Road site plan compliance
200-turnpike-road.description: Site plan compliance, occupancy permitting, and landscape performance bonding for a commercial facility at 200 Turnpike Road.
200-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board recommended the issuance of a full certificate of occupancy for 200 Turnpike Road after accepting a $30,000 landscaping performance bond and surety agreement in June 2026. Peer review found the commercial facility's civil construction compliant, with the bond covering replacement plantings and slope stabilization following winter erosion. A follow-up inspection is slated for fall 2027 to verify plant survival and stability before the bond agreement concludes.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026, to accept the $30,000 surety agreement and recommend a full certificate of occupancy.

200-turnpike-road.next: Follow-up inspection on plant survival and slope stability on October 1, 2027

2030-master-plan-update.name: 2030 Master Plan update
2030-master-plan-update.description: Strategy, funding, and consultant selection for updating Southborough's comprehensive Master Plan for 2030.
2030-master-plan-update.status: Early planning is underway for Southborough's 2030 comprehensive Master Plan, with the Master Plan Implementation Committee recommending a hybrid model pairing volunteer committee members with an outside consultant. The committee has proposed that the Planning Board take ownership of the update and establish a dedicated Master Plan 2030 committee in 2027. Key open questions include whether to finance estimated consultant costs of $50,000 to $100,000 through state technical assistance grants or a spring Town Meeting warrant article. The two boards will meet jointly on October 19, 2026, to review comparative research from neighboring towns and discuss next steps.

positions.detail: Recommends creating a dedicated Master Plan 2030 committee in 2027 and using a hybrid volunteer-consultant model funded by grants or a warrant article.
Has received initial briefings on the hybrid approach and committee structure, deferring formal discussion and goal adoption to a joint session.

2030-master-plan-update.next: Joint meeting between the Planning Board and the Master Plan Implementation Committee on October 19, 2026.

21-coslin-drive-costco.name: 21 Coslin Drive Costco development
21-coslin-drive-costco.description: Site plan and special permit review for a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco retail warehouse and 30-position gas station at 21 Coslin Drive.
21-coslin-drive-costco.status: The proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position fueling station is currently under major site plan and special permit review before the Planning Board, having received variance approvals from the Zoning Board of Appeals in July. Deliberations center on traffic impacts along Route 9, neighborhood cut-through routes on Flagg Road, truck turnaround access at Route 85, and site grading. The Planning Board's public hearing is scheduled to continue on October 19, 2026, following receipt of an independent traffic peer review.

positions.detail: Under review; opened the public hearing on site plan and special permit applications on Sept 28 and continued review pending traffic peer evaluation.
Voted 4-0 on July 15 to grant variances for retaining wall heights up to 31 feet and light pole heights of 36.5 feet.
Residents voiced concerns regarding severe Route 9 congestion, cut-through traffic on Flagg and Southville roads, truck turnaround safety at Route 85, and water pressure.

21-coslin-drive-costco.next: Planning Board public hearing on October 19, 2026

21-highland-street-use.name: 21 Highland Street future use
21-highland-street-use.description: Planning for municipal department space allocation, community use, or potential sale of the town-owned building at 21 Highland Street.
21-highland-street-use.status: The Recreation Department is preparing to expand into space at 21 Highland Street as Youth and Family Services completes its relocation to the Flagg School in late October. Plans for the vacated space include after-school STEM and arts programming rooms as well as a shared evening meeting space for civic boards. Broader questions about the building's long-term future remain open following earlier Select Board goal-setting discussions regarding a potential sale of the property.

positions.detail: Supports repurposing space vacated by Youth and Family Services for department offices, after-school activities, and community meeting use.

22-newton-street-variance.name: 22 Newton Street garage variance
22-newton-street-variance.description: Variance petition under Section 174-8.3(D)(3)(b) to construct a detached two-car garage encroaching on side lot line setbacks at 22 Newton Street.
22-newton-street-variance.status: The variance petition for 22 Newton Street has been withdrawn without prejudice. The Zoning Board of Appeals approved the withdrawal in June 2026 after board members raised concerns that the garage would sit on the side lot line and block access required for septic repairs. The homeowner is reconsidering design options, and no revised application has been filed.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 10 to approve the applicant's withdrawal without prejudice following concerns regarding zero-foot setbacks and septic maintenance access.

22-turnpike-road.name: 22 Turnpike Road site plan modification
22-turnpike-road.description: Site plan modification to expand stormwater infiltration, permit existing patios and a shed, and address sports lighting at 22 Turnpike Road.
22-turnpike-road.status: The proposed major site plan modification for the 22 Turnpike Road golf driving range is under Planning Board review while a draft decision is prepared. The Conservation Commission approved a negative determination of applicability for a storage shed on the property in April 2026. The Planning Board will take up the draft decision at its continued hearing on October 19, 2026, ahead of an October 23 decision deadline.

positions.detail: Has repeatedly continued the hearing while reviewing revised submissions and is awaiting a draft decision.
Voted 5-0 on April 30, 2026, to issue a negative determination of applicability with standard conditions for an equipment storage shed.

22-turnpike-road.next: Planning Board continued public hearing to review draft decision on October 19, 2026.

229-parkerville-road-coc.name: 229 Parkerville Road Certificate of Compliance
229-parkerville-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review and buffer zone encroachment resolution for a fenced garden at 229 Parkerville Road.
229-parkerville-road-coc.status: The Certificate of Compliance remains pending a final site inspection by the conservation agent scheduled for fall 2026. The Conservation Commission and the homeowner agreed on a resolution allowing an existing split-rail fence to stay in place as the permanent work limit while requiring garden trellises extending past the fence to be dismantled. Once staff confirms on-site that the encroaching trellises have been removed to allow natural revegetation, the certificate is expected to be issued.

positions.detail: Agreed on June 4 to allow the split-rail fence to remain, conditioning issuance of the certificate on the removal of encroaching garden trellises verified by a fall site visit.

229-parkerville-road-coc.next: Conservation agent site visit in fall 2026.

250-turnpike-road.name: 250 Turnpike Road 40B development
250-turnpike-road.description: Comprehensive permit application under Chapter 40B for residential development at 250 Turnpike Road.
250-turnpike-road.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a comprehensive permit for the 32-unit Chapter 40B townhouse development in May 2026, but environmental and site-level reviews remain underway. The Conservation Commission is currently reviewing the Notice of Intent, which was continued in October while awaiting an environmental peer review. The Board of Health approved a setback variance for a septic pump chamber in September, though broader wastewater replacement and wetland crossing plans still require state and local approvals.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on May 6, 2026 to approve the comprehensive permit and waivers with conditions for the 32-unit townhouse development.
Continued the Notice of Intent hearing on Oct 8, 2026 while awaiting a peer review from Lucas Environmental.
Voted 2-1 on Sep 15, 2026 to approve a 6-foot foundation setback variance for a replacement septic pump chamber.
Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026 to recommend a 90-day extension of the temporary certificate of occupancy for the on-site storage facility.

34-turnpike-road-special-permit.name: 34 Turnpike Road special permit
34-turnpike-road-special-permit.description: Special permit review and zoning compliance for unpermitted construction and renovations exceeding approvals at 34 Turnpike Road.
34-turnpike-road-special-permit.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved 1.3 feet of side setback relief for the as-built addition at 34 Turnpike Road, subject to Board of Health certification that the septic system accommodates the bedroom count. The applicant must also cut back an unauthorized foundation bump-out at grade to resolve a septic setback encroachment. The approval followed neighbor objections over dwelling size and septic capacity.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 10 to approve side setback relief on the condition that the Board of Health verifies adequate septic capacity.
A representative for an abutting owner opposed the zoning relief, arguing the expanded structure exceeds permitted size and lacks certified septic capacity.

355-turnpike-road-coc.name: 355 Turnpike Road Certificate of Compliance
355-turnpike-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review, unapproved paving, and stormwater maintenance for a commercial site at 355 Turnpike Road.
355-turnpike-road-coc.status: The request for a Certificate of Compliance for 355 Turnpike Road remains on hold pending site cleanup and additional documentation. An August 2026 inspection revealed unapproved pavement expansion, catch basins showing an oil sheen, and an uncleared stormwater outlet, preventing the release of the order of conditions. The Conservation Commission maintained the matter on its agenda in September without taking action while awaiting required maintenance and engineering clarification.

positions.detail: Tabled the certificate of compliance request pending required site cleanup, catch basin maintenance, and engineering clarification regarding unpermitted paving.

40-42-central-street.name: 40-42 Central Street site plan compliance
40-42-central-street.description: Resolution of site plan discrepancies, parking configurations, and occupancy permitting for 40-42 Central Street.
40-42-central-street.status: Site plan compliance and occupancy permitting for 40-42 Central Street remain unresolved while the applicant completes paving and awaits town inspection of required accessible parking spaces. The Zoning Board of Appeals is considering an appeal of the building commissioner's denial of a certificate of occupancy and zoning violation notice. Meanwhile, the Planning Board previously recommended revoking the property's temporary certificate of occupancy and discussed threatened litigation from the owner. The Zoning Board of Appeals takes up the continued appeal on October 21, 2026.

positions.detail: Continued the hearing to October 21 to allow completion and inspection of accessible parking spaces required by the building commissioner.
Voted 4-1 on May 11 to recommend revoking the temporary certificate of occupancy and held an executive session in June regarding threatened litigation from the owner.

40-42-central-street.next: Zoning Board of Appeals continued hearing on October 21, 2026 at 7:00 PM.

55-plus-housing-bylaw.name: 55-plus housing zoning bylaw amendment
55-plus-housing-bylaw.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendment to eliminate caps on age-restricted 55-plus developments and clarify affordability requirements.
55-plus-housing-bylaw.status: The Affordable Housing Trust is drafting proposed amendments to the town's 55-plus housing bylaw to eliminate the total cap on age-restricted units and require a 12.5 percent affordability mandate. Trustees are also considering density controls, including a potential two-acre minimum lot size under special permits, based on earlier public hearing feedback and input from the town planner and Zoning Board of Appeals. A revised draft is scheduled for review by the Trust in October 2026 ahead of Town Counsel review and submission to Annual Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Drafting amendments to remove the townwide unit cap and establish a mandatory 12.5 percent affordability requirement for new 55-plus developments.

55-plus-housing-bylaw.next: Review of revised draft bylaw at the Affordable Housing Trust meeting in October 2026.

6-walker-street-variance.name: 6 Walker Street garage setback variance
6-walker-street-variance.description: Petition to modify a 1965 variance condition and grant a 6.5-foot side setback variance to construct a garage addition at 6 Walker Street.
6-walker-street-variance.status: The requested variance modification and setback relief have been approved. On July 15, 2026, the Zoning Board of Appeals voted unanimously to amend a 1965 variance condition and grant a 6.5-foot side setback variance for an attached garage addition at 6 Walker Street. With the public hearing closed and relief granted, no further board approvals are pending.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on July 15, 2026, to amend the 1965 variance condition and approve the 6.5-foot side setback variance based on site and septic constraints.
Abutters submitted letters of support for the project, and no opposition was voiced at the hearing.

65c-school-street-coc.name: 65C School Street Certificate of Compliance
65c-school-street-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review following unpermitted brush clearing and wetland buffer zone remediation at 65C School Street.
65c-school-street-coc.status: The Conservation Commission approved a Certificate of Compliance for 65C School Street on July 29, 2026, resolving the matter. The approval followed the homeowner's remediation of an unpermitted brush clearing within the 20-foot no-touch wetland buffer zone. With native plantings completed and an updated as-built plan submitted, no further regulatory action is required.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on July 29, 2026, to issue the Certificate of Compliance following completed buffer zone restoration.

66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.name: 66 Breakneck Hill Road septic variance
66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.description: Septic system upgrade and wetland setback variance to support converting a commercial building to residential use at 66 Breakneck Hill Road.
66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved a septic variance for 66 Breakneck Hill Road to support converting a commercial property into a four-bedroom single-family residence. The decision permits an 85-foot wetland setback instead of the standard 100 feet, which improves upon the existing 79-foot setback and requires a nitrogen-reducing treatment unit. The project now awaits review and approval by the Conservation Commission.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Oct 13 to approve the wetland setback variance with an advanced nitrogen-reducing unit, contingent on Conservation Commission review.

7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.name: 7 Turnpike Road bodywork compliance
7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.description: Town bodywork permitting compliance and cease-and-desist enforcement for an unlicensed massage business operating at 7 Turnpike Road.
7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.status: The Board of Health unanimously denied an establishment license application for the Turnpike Road bodywork business following repeated compliance failures and an active cease-and-desist order. Health department staff and town counsel were authorized to draft and execute a formal written decision denying the permit. No further hearings or town actions are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on August 11 to deny the establishment license application, citing operation during a cease-and-desist order and missing practitioner credentials.

8-partridge-hill-road-variance.name: 8 Partridge Hill Road septic variance
8-partridge-hill-road-variance.description: Septic repair variance regarding groundwater separation and setback to the Sudbury Reservoir at 8 Partridge Hill Road.
8-partridge-hill-road-variance.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved septic repair variances for 8 Partridge Hill Road on August 11, 2026. The decision grants relief from local groundwater separation and setback requirements to the Sudbury Reservoir to replace a failed 1975 system. With no state conservation objections raised, the matter is concluded and no further board action is scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on Aug 11 to approve variances for the replacement system, noting the state voiced no objections and design flow remains unchanged.

911-field-bond-and-fees.name: 911 Field bond repayment and fees
911-field-bond-and-fees.description: Debt service repayment schedule and revolving fund athletic field user fees for the 911 Field turf complex.
911-field-bond-and-fees.status: The Recreation Commission is reviewing adjusted debt service schedules and a potential $5-per-hour field user fee increase to repay the remaining turf bond for the 911 Field complex. Annual revolving fund revenues have fallen short of initial projections, prompting discussions of extending $30,000 to $45,000 annual installments through FY35. The commission deferred formal action pending refined revenue models and fee proposals from the recreation and finance directors.

positions.detail: Weighing an extended debt payback plan and a modest fee increase for fall leagues, deferring a decision until updated financial projections are provided.

appointed-town-clerk.name: Appointed town clerk transition
appointed-town-clerk.description: Proposal to transition the town clerk from an elected office to an appointed position, including interim clerk appointments.
appointed-town-clerk.status: A proposal to transition the town clerk from an elected office to an appointed position goes before Special Town Meeting as Article 1, with unanimous endorsements from both the Select Board and the Advisory Committee. Supporters cite the need to recruit qualified applicants from outside Southborough for an increasingly technical position, though committee members noted concerns regarding the loss of direct voter control. If approved at Town Meeting, the charter change will require final approval by voters at the May 11, 2027 annual town election.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 to recommend approval of Article 1 and appointed an interim clerk through May 2027.
Voted 6-0 to recommend approval to expand the applicant pool, while advising that future employment contracts include termination-for-cause protections.

appointed-town-clerk.next: Special Town Meeting vote on Article 1 on October 17, 2026

board-of-health-body-art-regulations.name: Board of Health body art regulations
board-of-health-body-art-regulations.description: Revisions to municipal body art regulations regarding practitioner training, apprenticeships, and prohibited activities.
board-of-health-body-art-regulations.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved updated local body art regulations in June 2026. The revised rules align with state model language by setting standards for apprenticeships, requiring practitioner training in CPR, first aid, anatomy, and bloodborne pathogens, and prohibiting vaping in procedure areas. With the vote concluded, the regulations are now established as local enforceable rules.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on June 9 to approve the revised regulations, including an amendment adding vaping to prohibited activities in procedure areas.

breakneck-hill-restoration.name: Breakneck Hill Conservation Land restoration
breakneck-hill-restoration.description: Planning and invasive species management for a comprehensive five-zone ecological restoration at Breakneck Hill Conservation Land.
breakneck-hill-restoration.status: The Stewardship Committee is developing a comprehensive five-zone ecological restoration and invasive species management plan for Breakneck Hill Conservation Land alongside the town planner. The town recovered $47,000 from remediation contractors to repair damaged sections of the beecology research meadow, which will require mechanical intervention for soil compaction before replanting. A formal scope of work is being drafted to solicit bids for botanical surveys, site grading, and native seeding.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Aug 4 to appoint a contractor liaison and is drafting a formal scope of work for comprehensive site restoration.

brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.name: Brox asphalt plant complaints
brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.description: Intermunicipal response and MassDEP oversight regarding resident noise and odor complaints concerning the Brox Industries asphalt plant in Marlborough.
brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.status: Southborough continues to monitor noise and odor complaints concerning the Brox Industries asphalt plant in Marlborough, though Town Counsel has advised that the town lacks regulatory jurisdiction over the out-of-town facility. While MassDEP found the plant meets emissions standards and Brox recently installed an exhaust mitigation system, nearby residents continue to report odors. Health officials are advising residents to submit detailed real-time logs directly to MassDEP to help regulators identify operational patterns.

positions.detail: Monitoring resident reports and coordinating with MassDEP while acknowledging the town lacks legal enforcement authority over the Marlborough plant.
Residents reported persistent chemical odors and early-morning noise, with one neighbor urging both towns to fund an independent air quality study.

cannabis-delivery-opt-out.name: Cannabis delivery opt-out waiver
cannabis-delivery-opt-out.description: Deliberation on whether Southborough should request a state waiver from the Cannabis Control Commission to prohibit adult-use cannabis home delivery.
cannabis-delivery-opt-out.status: Adult-use cannabis home delivery is permitted in Southborough after the Select Board voted against seeking a state opt-out waiver. The Board of Health previously reviewed the waiver but declined to take a formal position, citing conflicting views on youth exposure and parity with alcohol delivery. No further action is planned, allowing state-licensed couriers to deliver to verified adult residents.

positions.detail: Voted 1-4 on Aug 11 against requesting a two-year opt-out waiver, leaving retail home delivery permitted for adults aged 21 and older.
Declined to take a formal stance on July 7, instead sending a memo outlining split member opinions on youth health risks versus parity with alcohol delivery.
A resident supported opting out, questioning whether courier ID checks would be reliably enforced and arguing delivery offers no public benefit.

cemetery-expansion.name: Town cemetery expansion planning
cemetery-expansion.description: Site evaluation and capacity planning to identify and acquire land for a new municipal cemetery.
cemetery-expansion.status: The ad hoc Cemetery Expansion Committee is evaluating 58 potential town and private parcels of five or more acres to identify land for a new municipal cemetery. Middle Road Cemetery has 458 plots remaining and is projected to reach capacity around 2035 or 2036, while Rural Cemetery is already sold out. The Select Board supports the effort and voted in September 2026 to downsize the committee to three members to help maintain meeting quorums. The committee is finalizing its screening matrix and expects to present site recommendations before June 2027.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to reduce the Cemetery Expansion Committee's membership to three to ensure consistent meeting quorums.

cemetery-expansion.next: Cemetery Expansion Committee presentation of final site recommendations before June 2027

classification-and-compensation-study.name: Municipal classification and compensation study
classification-and-compensation-study.description: A comprehensive classification and compensation study evaluating 48 non-union municipal employee positions.
classification-and-compensation-study.status: A comprehensive classification and compensation study of 48 non-union municipal positions is currently underway by consultant MGT, with survey data collection from peer communities wrapping up. The Personnel Board has put all individual job reclassification requests on hold until the townwide review is completed. Recommendations from the study are expected to go before voters at the Annual Town Meeting in March 2027.

positions.detail: Commissioned the study and is pausing individual reclassifications to evaluate all 48 positions collectively once consultant findings are delivered.
A municipal employee expressed concern over the board's vote to exclude Dover from the peer survey list, urging adherence to the independent consultant's process.

classification-and-compensation-study.next: Presentation of study recommendations at the Annual Town Meeting in March 2027

conservation-land-use-regulations.name: Conservation land use regulations
conservation-land-use-regulations.description: Adoption and amendment of town code regulations governing public use and activities on town-owned conservation land.
conservation-land-use-regulations.status: The Conservation Commission adopted regulations governing town-owned conservation land under Section 43-2 of the Southborough Town Code in April 2026. The regulations incorporated feedback from the Breakneck Hill Stewardship Committee and were filed with the town clerk. The commission noted that future amendments may be considered to address issues such as light trespass from abutting parcels.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on April 30, 2026, to formally adopt the land use regulations under Town Code Section 43-2.

constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.name: Constitution Drive drainage and street acceptance
constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.description: Sinkhole repair at 11 Constitution Drive and resolution of unrecorded municipal street and drainage easements.
constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.status: The Select Board has authorized the Department of Public Works to perform an estimated $5,000 repair on a recurring driveway sinkhole at 11 Constitution Drive, subject to a homeowner hold-harmless agreement. An investigation found that although Town Meeting approved the road and easements in the past, deeds were never recorded, leaving the street and drainage easements legally unaccepted. Town staff and town counsel are currently investigating the legal steps required to rectify the street and easement acceptance.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Sep 2 to approve the one-time driveway repair and directed town counsel and staff to resolve the unrecorded street and drainage easements.

costco-special-act-liquor-license.name: Costco special act liquor license
costco-special-act-liquor-license.description: Proposed special state legislation authorizing an additional off-premises liquor license in Southborough for Costco.
costco-special-act-liquor-license.status: Special state legislation to authorize an additional off-premises liquor license for Costco remains pending at the State House. The proposed language allows the town two years to award the license and includes a three-year sunset clause if it goes unused. The Select Board supports the measure and agreed to submit testimony backing the bill following a legislative hearing held in June.

positions.detail: Agreed on June 16 to submit written testimony in favor of the special legislation.

culvert-infrastructure-replacements.name: Culvert infrastructure replacements
culvert-infrastructure-replacements.description: Town-wide culvert replacements funded through a state grant to replace previously authorized borrowing.
culvert-infrastructure-replacements.status: Town culvert replacement work is proceeding after Southborough secured nearly $3.9 million from the Massachusetts Community Culvert Grant Program, replacing previously authorized town debt. In August, the Select Board approved three permanent private drainage easements along Willow Street required for permitting and construction access. The town is expected to eventually bring the original borrowing authorization back to Town Meeting to be rescinded.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on August 11, 2026, to accept three private drainage easements needed to advance the Willow Street culvert project.

downtown-wayfinding-plan.name: Downtown Southborough Wayfinding Plan
downtown-wayfinding-plan.description: A state grant-funded planning study to design and install directional, gateway, and informational signage across downtown Southborough.
downtown-wayfinding-plan.status: The draft Downtown Southborough Wayfinding Plan is under review as the town seeks state grant funding to develop fabrication specifications and install signage. Both the Select Board and the Historical Commission have asked consultants to include omitted historic landmarks and favor simpler sign designs. The Historical Commission has also raised concerns about modern suburban aesthetics and visual clutter along the downtown corridor.

positions.detail: Voiced concerns over visual sign clutter and suburban-style designs, while urging that key sites like the Community House and Burnett Mansion be included.
Received the consultant's presentation in June and recommended simpler designs alongside the inclusion of missing historic destinations.

fay-school-25-middle-road.name: Fay School 25 Middle Road addition
fay-school-25-middle-road.description: Review of as-built plans, construction discrepancies, and landscape mitigation for an addition at Fay School's 25 Middle Road campus.
fay-school-25-middle-road.status: Fay School's addition at 25 Middle Road is under review by the Planning Board as the school works to satisfy conditions required for a final certificate of occupancy. The school has submitted updated landscape mitigation plans to replace removed trees and correct past plantings of non-native cultivars. The board is awaiting completion of an engineering peer review on as-built plans and confirmation of native, pesticide-free plantings before finalizing an agreement.

positions.detail: Previously recommended a temporary certificate of occupancy in August and is reviewing updated landscaping plans and pending engineering peer reviews before granting final sign-off.
A resident urged that mitigation plantings be certified free of neonicotinoid pesticides, strictly native, and accompanied by eradication of invasive species.

fay-school-athletic-fields.name: Fay School athletic fields redevelopment
fay-school-athletic-fields.description: Notice of Intent and redevelopment to convert grass soccer fields to artificial turf and relocate a baseball field at Fay School's 0 Marlboro Junction property.
fay-school-athletic-fields.status: The Conservation Commission is reviewing a Notice of Intent and stormwater management permit to convert grass fields to artificial turf and reconstruct athletic fields at Fay School's 0 Marlborough Junction property. The public hearing has been repeatedly continued at the applicant's request without substantive presentations. The commission has not yet evaluated the proposal on its merits.

positions.detail: Has continued the public hearing across multiple meetings at the applicant's request without substantive discussion on the merits.

fayville-memorial-park-improvements.name: Fayville Memorial Park improvements
fayville-memorial-park-improvements.description: Planning, community outreach, and design improvements for Fayville Memorial Park, including splash pad features and parking capacity.
fayville-memorial-park-improvements.status: The proposed park renovation and parking expansion is under review, with the project's Community Preservation Act funding request deferred to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting. The Recreation Commission is pursuing an angled on-street parking layout along Central Street to preserve interior green space, while officials evaluate traffic sight lines and potential Article 97 conservation restrictions near the reservoir. The town is also awaiting an announcement on a federal grant that could cover roughly $609,000 of the estimated $1.5 million project cost.

positions.detail: Favors advancing the park redesign with angled parking along Central Street to protect park trees, and is consulting town counsel on open-space restrictions.
Reviewed the angled parking proposal on Sep 2 without taking a formal vote, requesting additional engineering data on site lines and vehicle buffers.
Residents raised safety concerns about fast traffic and blind spots from angled parking on Central Street, while also asking about crosswalk safety and proposed dog park regulations.

flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.name: Flagg Road and Route 9 hydrant relocation
flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.description: Relocation of a frequently struck fire hydrant and removal of scenic road stone wall at Flagg Road and 361 Turnpike Road.
flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.status: The project is approved to move forward after the Planning Board granted permission to dismantle approximately 10 feet of scenic road stone wall. The removal allows the Department of Public Works to relocate a frequently struck fire hydrant roughly 10 feet back into a newly acquired utility easement. Approval was granted with conditions requiring the removed stones to remain on Flagg Road or be reused in adjacent wall restoration.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on May 11, 2026, to approve the stone wall removal on the condition that removed stones remain on Flagg Road or be reused for wall reconstruction.

fy27-road-paving-contracts.name: FY27 road paving and sidewalk contracts
fy27-road-paving-contracts.description: Procurement and contract awards for fiscal year 2027 DPW road paving and sidewalk maintenance.
fy27-road-paving-contracts.status: The Select Board unanimously approved the contract awards for fiscal year 2027 road paving and sidewalk maintenance on September 15, 2026. The paving contract covers six roads, including interim work on sections of Cordaville Road and Cranberry Road, with bids coming in approximately $400,000 below engineering estimates. The contracts are now finalized to proceed for FY27.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to approve the FY27 road paving and sidewalk contracts after bids came in well below engineering estimates.

fy27-school-operating-budget.name: FY27 school operating budget
fy27-school-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, class size staffing, and reserve funding for the Southborough K-8 public schools for fiscal year 2027.
fy27-school-operating-budget.status: Following approval of the FY27 budget, the district received $105,485 more in state Chapter 70 education aid than originally projected. In September 2026, the School Committee asked the Select Board to deposit these surplus funds into the town's Special Education Stabilization Fund, which currently has a zero balance. The transfer now awaits action by the Select Board.

positions.detail: Endorsed a 3.99% FY27 operating budget increase in May 2026 and agreed in September to request placing $105,485 in unexpected Chapter 70 aid into the Special Education Stabilization Fund.

fy28-operating-budget.name: FY28 operating budget
fy28-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, multi-year deficit forecasting, and consideration of a Proposition 2 1/2 operational override for fiscal year 2028.
fy28-operating-budget.status: Town officials are preparing the FY28 operating budget against a projected structural deficit exceeding $2 million, leading the Select Board and Advisory Committee to evaluate a potential Proposition 2 1/2 operational override. Departments were instructed to submit dual budget proposals—one maintaining level services with a recommended 5 percent salary increase, and one flat-funded requiring service and staffing cuts. The town faces key decisions on whether to pursue a multi-year override at the ballot, with joint budget reviews scheduled to begin in November ahead of an earlier March 2027 Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Issued dual-budget guidelines to department heads while studying a potential multi-year operational override of up to five years to cover the projected deficit.
Urged caution regarding a multi-year override, advocating for stricter spending controls, departmental efficiency reviews, and a potential hiring freeze before asking voters for additional taxes.
Voted 4-0 on Sep 8 to recommend a 5 percent overall salary adjustment for FY28, combining a 3 percent cost-of-living increase with step increments.
Voted 6-0 on Oct 5 to approve its FY28 operating budget, warning that flat funding if an override fails would drastically reduce subscriptions and eliminate programming.
Voted unanimously on Oct 7 to approve a $4,250 operating budget request after clarifying trail mowing contracts with the Department of Public Works.
Approved its small elected board budget but postponed action on its departmental budget to Oct 20 while weighing staff hour reductions required under a zero-increase scenario.
Postponed formal action on its budget memo after members voiced frustration that flat-budget guidelines would require cutting the conservation agent's hours.
Residents suggested consolidating departmental budgets to improve efficiency, while cautioning that altering line-item budget presentations could heighten voter skepticism in an override year.

fy28-operating-budget.next: Board of Health vote on its departmental operating budget on October 20, 2026.

glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.name: Glow SoBo holiday lighting
glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.description: Funding and municipal installation of holiday lighting displays and kickoff event for the Tricentennial.
glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.status: Plans for the Glow SoBo holiday lighting display are moving forward following municipal funding and site approvals. The Tricentennial Committee approved a $10,456 professional lighting contract for the Town House, library, and surrounding trees, and library trustees consented to decorations and permanent outdoor electrical work on their grounds. Decisions regarding whether to host indoor open-house activities at the library remain deferred ahead of the planned kickoff in early December.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on Aug 12 to approve a $10,456 contract for professional exterior holiday lighting on town buildings and trees.
Voted unanimously on Sep 14 to approve exterior decorations and permanent electrical outlet installation funded by the Tricentennial Committee.

hopkinton-water-connection.name: Hopkinton MWRA water connection
hopkinton-water-connection.description: Proposed intermunicipal agreement to convey MWRA water to the town of Hopkinton through Southborough's distribution system.
hopkinton-water-connection.status: The proposed intermunicipal agreement to convey MWRA water to Hopkinton through Southborough's distribution system is currently under review after negotiations resumed following a stall in 2023. The Select Board has received an update on the agreement's terms—which include a $1 million payment to Southborough, street repaving, and replacing the Oak Hill Road water tank—but has not yet taken a formal stance. Key upcoming steps include Hopkinton obtaining state approvals, Southborough hiring an independent engineering firm for design review, and appointing special municipal counsel to negotiate the contract.

housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.name: Housing and food health code enforcement policies
housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.description: Board of Health standardized enforcement procedures, violation correction timelines, and fee schedules for housing and food establishments.
housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.status: The Board of Health is reviewing updated enforcement policies and fee schedules for repeat health code violations in housing and food establishments. The board tabled formal approval in August 2026 to allow staff to add clearer language specifying how compliance deadlines are determined based on violation severity. Revised drafts were expected in September, but no formal vote has been taken and no follow-up discussion is currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Tabled formal approval on August 11, 2026, requesting clearer language on how violation severity will dictate compliance deadlines.

kallander-field-repairs.name: Kallander Field turf repairs
kallander-field-repairs.description: Scoping, vendor pricing, and DPW coordination for repairing turf and playing surface conditions at Kallander Field.
kallander-field-repairs.status: Repair plans for Kallander Field remain under review by the Recreation Commission. The original turf installer proposed completing the work for $8,000 to $9,000 with Department of Public Works assistance, well below earlier $40,000 estimates and within the commission's available capital funds. The commission discussed the proposal in May 2026 but had not yet taken formal action.

positions.detail: Reviewed an $8,000 to $9,000 repair estimate from the original turf installer in May 2026 but deferred formal action.

kratom-retail-ban.name: Statewide kratom ban and local enforcement
kratom-retail-ban.description: Local Board of Health enforcement and retail monitoring following the state's Schedule I temporary ban on kratom.
kratom-retail-ban.status: Southborough health staff have reviewed local retailers following a statewide one-year order that classified kratom as a Schedule I controlled substance in August 2026. Staff found only one local retailer carrying a small display of kratom and provided education on securing, returning, or lawfully disposing of remaining stock. The Board of Health received an informational update in September 2026, with no board action required.

landfill-environmental-assessment.name: Southborough landfill environmental assessment
landfill-environmental-assessment.description: Environmental risk assessment, private well testing, and potential municipal water line extension regarding contamination from the Southborough landfill.
landfill-environmental-assessment.status: Article 7 is headed to Special Town Meeting to appropriate $240,000 from water retained earnings to extend a municipal water main and connect two homes near the closed Parkerville Road landfill. Both the Select Board and Advisory Committee support the project to eliminate contamination risks and avoid perpetual state-mandated private well monitoring. Voters will decide on the appropriation, which covers running the water main and service lines directly into both residences.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on Oct 6 to recommend Article 7 after confirming the town will cover the service lines from the street into the residences.
Supported placing the water service extension on the warrant to permanently address landfill contamination risks and bypass state testing mandates.

latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.name: Latisquama Road errant golf balls
latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.description: Safety concerns and mitigation options regarding errant golf balls striking residential properties on Latisquama Road from the Southborough Golf Club.
latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.status: The Golf Committee is evaluating options to mitigate errant golf balls hitting homes along Latisquama Road from the Southborough Golf Club's 7th hole. Discussed remedies include relocating the tee box, converting the hole into a par 3, or reorienting the green. The committee plans to seek input from a golf architect on potential redesign options.

positions.detail: Agreed to consult a golf architect on potential redesigns for the 7th hole after debating options including moving the tee or shortening the hole.

library-book-drop-repair.name: Library book drop concrete repair
library-book-drop-repair.description: Repair and funding of damaged concrete beneath the Southborough Library book drop and clarification of municipal maintenance responsibilities.
library-book-drop-repair.status: Repairs to the concrete platform beneath the Southborough Library book drop were scheduled for early October 2026 using under $5,000 in library State Aid funds. The Library Board of Trustees funded the project directly to resolve a tripping hazard and drainage issue following uncertainty over whether the work fell under library or DPW jurisdiction. The trustees also authorized a letter to town officials to establish clear boundaries for future exterior grounds maintenance.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously in May 2026 to fund the concrete replacement through State Aid and to request clear municipal maintenance boundaries from town officials.

library-cpa-signage.name: Library CPA commemorative signage
library-cpa-signage.description: Design and wording of commemorative plaques crediting Community Preservation Act funding for Southborough Library restoration projects.
library-cpa-signage.status: Design and wording for two plaques acknowledging Community Preservation Act funding at the Southborough Library have been finalized and approved. The Community Preservation Committee and the Library Board of Trustees agreed to credit the 'residents of Southborough' and feature the town seal rather than the library logo. The signs have been commissioned, and invoices have been submitted to the CPC for payment.

positions.detail: Voted 5-1 on July 21 to approve plaque wording crediting the 'residents of Southborough' with the town seal.
Advocated successfully for crediting 'residents' rather than 'taxpayers' and commissioned the approved signs.

library-parking-lot-repaving.name: Library parking lot repaving
library-parking-lot-repaving.description: Capital planning, DPW coordination, and town warrant sponsorship for repaving the Southborough Library parking lot.
library-parking-lot-repaving.status: The proposed repaving and replacement of the library parking lot has been deferred and will not be submitted as an FY28 capital request. Facilities assessments determined that required site engineering to protect the water table and manage runoff makes the work too costly to fund in the near term. The project is instead slated to be proposed for town capital planning in two to three years.

positions.detail: Agreed to postpone the capital request for two to three years after drainage and water table engineering drove up the project's projected cost.

mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.name: McAuliffe Hearing Room audiovisual upgrades
mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.description: Hardware, camera framing, and video conferencing upgrades for hybrid public meetings in the McAuliffe Hearing Room at the Town House.
mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.status: Hardware and software upgrades in the McAuliffe Hearing Room are largely in place and undergoing fine-tuning. Recent adjustments have addressed front desk monitor sightlines and microphone calibration, though displaying remote attendee lists to in-person audiences and configuring Zoom webinar controls remain open items. The Municipal Technology Committee is continuing to monitor user feedback as technicians troubleshoot the system.

positions.detail: Supports the ongoing hybrid meeting upgrades and continues to gather feedback while technicians resolve remaining display and software issues.

metrowest-recc-borrowing.name: MetroWest RECC borrowing authorization
metrowest-recc-borrowing.description: Short-term borrowing authorization of up to $12.5 million to bridge state grant funding for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center.
metrowest-recc-borrowing.status: The Select Board approved up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing authority in May 2026 to serve as bridge financing between state 911 grant disbursements for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center. The authorization aligned Southborough with partner towns Grafton and Westborough, despite debate over taking on regional borrowing risk. Outstanding resident concerns focus on municipal exposure to ongoing lease, legal, and insurance expenses.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on May 19 to approve up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing notes to keep construction on schedule, over one member's objection to assuming regional debt risk.
A resident raised concerns regarding town liability for leasehold improvements, legal fees, and insurance costs under the regional lease agreement.

municipal-grants-management-policy.name: Municipal Grants Management Policy
municipal-grants-management-policy.description: Town oversight and approval procedures governing municipal grant applications, match funding, and operational liabilities.
municipal-grants-management-policy.status: The Municipal Grants Management Policy was adopted following unanimous approval by the Select Board in April 2026. The policy sets municipal oversight and approval procedures for grant applications, local match funding, and ongoing operational liabilities. No further board reviews or updates are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on April 28, 2026, to approve the Grants Management Financial Policy as amended.

municipal-health-insurance-reform.name: Municipal employee health insurance reform
municipal-health-insurance-reform.description: Adoption of MGL Chapter 32B Sections 21-23 and collective bargaining with the Public Employee Committee to modify municipal health insurance plans.
municipal-health-insurance-reform.status: The town is preparing to enter expedited negotiations with the Public Employee Committee after the Select Board voted to adopt MGL Chapter 32B, Sections 21 through 23. Southborough is coordinating with Northborough and the regional school district to pursue health insurance plan design changes to lower premium costs, which represent 11.2 percent of the municipal budget. Any negotiated modifications are intended to take effect on July 1, 2027.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on August 11, 2026, to adopt MGL Chapter 32B Sections 21–23 to allow expedited negotiations over municipal health plan design changes.

national-grid-vegetation-plan.name: National Grid FY27 vegetation management plan
national-grid-vegetation-plan.description: Annual review and approval of National Grid's tree pruning and vegetation management plan along town distribution circuits.
national-grid-vegetation-plan.status: National Grid's FY27 vegetation management plan is approved following endorsement by the Planning Board and town tree warden in August 2026. The work covers routine clearance pruning along distribution circuits on Parmenter Road, Pine Hill Road, Nichols Street, and Clemmons Street. No full tree removals are included under the routine maintenance plan, with any hazardous trees requiring separate joint hearings.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on Aug 17 to approve the FY27 vegetation management plan.
Concurred on Aug 17 to approve the annual pruning plan alongside the Planning Board.
A resident questioned utility trimming specifications versus town standards and expressed concern about the aesthetic impact on roadside trees.

native-plant-landscape-regulations.name: Native plant landscape regulations
native-plant-landscape-regulations.description: Proposed Planning Board site plan rules and regulations mandating native plantings and invasive species management.
native-plant-landscape-regulations.status: The Planning Board unanimously adopted the Native Landscape Regulations in May 2026 for all projects undergoing site plan review. The new rules require that all new plantings consist of native New England species and prohibit the use of neonicotinoid pesticides. A broader section addressing invasive species management was deferred for separate review.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on May 11, 2026, to adopt the amended native landscaping standards into site plan regulations.
Collaborated on and presented the draft policy requiring native plantings and pesticide restrictions to benefit pollinators and wildlife.

neary-school-building-project.name: Neary School building project
neary-school-building-project.description: Feasibility, design, and renovation or replacement planning for Neary Elementary School.
neary-school-building-project.status: The Elementary School Building Committee has narrowed its focus to a base renovation, a courtyard gymnasium infill, and a scoped $15 million repair baseline after voting to eliminate an exterior addition. With estimated total costs running between $24.4 million and $49.2 million, officials face challenges reconciling comprehensive educational improvements with earlier $15 million budget benchmarks. The committee is set to present its refined design options and preliminary costs to voters at Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Sep 24 to advance Options 1, 3, and a $15 million baseline scope to Town Meeting, after voting 3-1 to eliminate Option 4.
Approved the design contract in June, emphasizing that consultants must objectively evaluate project options without eliminating them before voters decide.
Voted to postpone its own athletic facility study until school planning concludes, while expressing concern over potential disruption to sports fields, parking, and gym availability.
Commenters urged officials to safeguard athletic fields and community gym access, while calling for full accounting of the costs to relocate central district offices.

neary-school-building-project.next: Presentation of Neary project options at Fall Town Meeting on October 17, 2026.

neary-school-roof-replacement.name: Neary School roof replacement
neary-school-roof-replacement.description: Proposed borrowing and debt exclusion to replace the failing roof and fund ADA upgrades at Neary Elementary School.
neary-school-roof-replacement.status: The Neary Elementary School roof replacement moved into construction over the summer of 2026 after combined low bids came in at approximately $2.8 million, well below the $4.5 million authorized by voters. Work was targeted for 85% to 90% completion before the start of the school year in late August. No further project milestones or hearings are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Advanced the project into summer construction after low bids totaled $2.8 million, well under the Town Meeting borrowing authorization.

opeb-funding-strategy.name: OPEB liability funding strategy
opeb-funding-strategy.description: Actuarial valuation, liability modeling, and long-term trust contribution strategy for the town's Other Post-Employment Benefits.
opeb-funding-strategy.status: Southborough's long-term OPEB funding strategy remains under review. The Select Board is examining ways to improve the town's roughly 8 percent funded ratio, including the potential reallocation of pension catch-up payments once the regional retirement system is fully funded around 2036. The board is awaiting actuarial models of multiple contribution scenarios before considering any policy changes.

positions.detail: Agreed in April to have actuaries model several future contribution scenarios to evaluate long-term funding targets.

parkerville-road-utility-pole.name: Parkerville Road utility pole petition
parkerville-road-utility-pole.description: Petition by National Grid and Verizon to install an additional utility pole between poles 101 and 102 on Parkerville Road.
parkerville-road-utility-pole.status: The utility pole petition has been approved by the town. The Select Board approved the petition in June 2026 after National Grid agreed to relocate the proposed pole approximately 1,000 feet away from direct abutters. Later that month, the Conservation Commission approved an Order of Conditions for the work in the right-of-way.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 16, 2026, to approve the petition after the proposed pole location was moved about 1,000 feet to an area without direct abutters.
Voted 5-0 on June 25, 2026, to approve an Order of Conditions with standard conditions, finding the roadside flood-storage displacement to be minimal.

peninsula-trail-phase-2.name: Peninsula Trail Phase 2
peninsula-trail-phase-2.description: Scope, wetland crossing design, and construction funding for Phase 2 of the Peninsula Trail.
peninsula-trail-phase-2.status: Article 4 heads to the Fall Special Town Meeting on October 17, 2026, requesting $217,318 in additional Community Preservation Act funds for a 65-foot prefabricated footbridge along Route 30. The supplemental request would bring total project funding to $428,550 after initial bids came in over budget and the project was redesigned. While the Community Preservation Committee, Trails Committee, Conservation Commission, and Recreation Commission back the project, both the Select Board and Advisory Committee strongly oppose it due to the estimated $5,000 per linear foot cost. Town Meeting voters will decide whether to approve the funding.

positions.detail: Voted 3-2 on Oct 8 to keep Article 4 on the warrant as printed, rejecting a proposed floor amendment to cut contingency funding.
Supports the full $217,318 funding request to resolve pedestrian safety hazards where the trail meets Route 30.
Voted 0-7 against the article, citing excessive costs of roughly $5,000 per linear foot despite recognizing safety concerns.
Voted 1-4 against recommending the article, expressing concern over the project's cost and prioritizing operating budget needs.
Voted 5-0 on June 25 to send a letter of support for the bridge's CPA application.
Voted 3-0 on June 30 to submit a letter of support for the updated footbridge funding application.

peninsula-trail-phase-2.next: Special Town Meeting vote on Article 4 on October 17, 2026.

personal-property-tax-exemption.name: Personal property tax exemption threshold
personal-property-tax-exemption.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article to raise Southborough's personal property tax exemption threshold from $1,500 to $2,500.
personal-property-tax-exemption.status: Article 8, which proposes raising Southborough's personal property tax exemption threshold from $1,500 to $2,500 beginning in fiscal year 2028, is awaiting Town Meeting. Both the Select Board and Advisory Committee unanimously support the change, citing administrative costs that exceed the tax revenue collected on roughly 22 small business accounts. The Advisory Committee recently finalized its warrant report wording to clarify the total assessed value of the exempt accounts.

positions.detail: Voted 7-0 on Sep 16 to recommend approval, finding that administrative collection expenses outweigh the minimal tax revenue.
Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to recommend approval of Article 8.

police-drone-program.name: Police Department drone program
police-drone-program.description: Proposed acquisition of a five-year police drone program package funded through unspent municipal personnel funds.
police-drone-program.status: The town has authorized the acquisition of a five-year police drone program, with the Municipal Technology Committee most recently recommending conditional approval for phased deployment. The Select Board voted to fund the $105,000 contract using surplus department personnel funds, offset by external contributions from Fay School and a state earmark. Implementation is moving forward under a pilot framework requiring pre-deployment verification and formal reviews after 90 days and 12 months.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Aug 27 to recommend conditional approval and phased deployment with formal reviews after 90 days and 12 months.
Approved the $105,000 purchase 3-2 on June 29 using surplus personnel funds, balancing immediate public safety needs against concerns about bypassing Town Meeting.
Voted 3-0 on June 24 to back the drone program as an immediate capital safety priority, deferring the year-end funding mechanism to the Select Board.

presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.name: Presidential and Fisher Road waterline looping
presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.description: MWRA loan funding and construction to connect dead-end water mains under CSX railroad tracks along Presidential Drive and Fisher Road.
presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.status: The waterline looping project along Presidential Drive and Fisher Road is moving forward after the Select Board unanimously approved a $1 million interest-free loan application to the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority in August 2026. Previously authorized by Town Meeting, the project will connect dead-end water mains beneath the CSX railroad tracks to improve water pressure and reduce bacterial buildup. The zero-interest financing is estimated to save the town more than $400,000 in interest costs compared to conventional borrowing.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on August 11, 2026, to authorize the $1 million zero-interest MWRA loan application.

rescinding-unissued-borrowing.name: Rescission of unissued borrowing authorizations
rescinding-unissued-borrowing.description: Proposed Special Town Meeting warrant article to rescind unused borrowing authorizations for completed capital projects, including Breakneck Hill and the Neary School study.
rescinding-unissued-borrowing.status: Article 6 for Special Town Meeting would rescind over $1.1 million in unused borrowing authority, covering $727,960 from the Breakneck Hill dump cleanup and $375,000 from the Neary School feasibility study. Both the Select Board and Advisory Committee support the article as an administrative measure to clear the town's books of unneeded debt authorization. However, the Conservation Commission has requested that the Select Board retain $100,000 of the Breakneck Hill borrowing capacity to help cover potential habitat and site restoration costs.

positions.detail: Voted 7-0 on Sep 16 to recommend approval, emphasizing that rescinding unused authority clears town books and prevents unneeded future debt.
Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to recommend approval of Article 6.
Voted 4-1 on Sep 17 to request reducing the rescission by $100,000 to preserve borrowing capacity for Breakneck Hill site and habitat restoration.

reserve-fund-transfer-policy.name: Reserve Fund transfer policy
reserve-fund-transfer-policy.description: Advisory Committee policy setting standard procedures, executive board oversight, and statutory criteria for departmental Reserve Fund transfer requests.
reserve-fund-transfer-policy.status: The Advisory Committee is updating its Reserve Fund transfer guidelines to establish formal procedures and statutory criteria for departmental requests. Under the draft policy, requests must be vetted by the town administrator and relevant executive boards, shared with the Capital Improvement Planning Committee for capital items, and limited to future, unforeseen expenses rather than retroactive reimbursements. Revisions were incorporated into a clean working draft in August awaiting final committee approval.

positions.detail: Drafting updated transfer guidelines to enforce statutory criteria, require prior administrative review, and prohibit retroactive reimbursements.

route-9-495-gateway-study.name: Route 9 and I-495 gateway corridor study
route-9-495-gateway-study.description: A joint $150,000 planning and infrastructure study with Westborough evaluating economic development, zoning, and infrastructure along the Route 9 and I-495 corridor.
route-9-495-gateway-study.status: A joint application with Westborough for a state Community One Stop for Growth grant to fund the $165,000 corridor study is currently awaiting a decision from the state. The Select Board, Planning Board, and Wastewater Study Committee all support the initiative, which would examine regional wastewater infrastructure, zoning, and economic development along Route 9. If the $150,000 state grant is awarded, Southborough and Westborough would each contribute a $7,500 local match to fund the engineering and planning work.

positions.detail: Helped prepare the joint application and is pausing consultant hiring and full meetings until grant awards are announced.
Voted 4-0 on May 21 to endorse the grant application after adjusting the support letter to protect residential buffers and emphasize commercial tax base growth.
Voted 5-0 on May 19 to approve an amended letter supporting the regional grant application.

route-9-495-gateway-study.next: State announcement of Community One Stop for Growth grant awards in October 2026

route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.name: Route 9 wastewater infrastructure plan
route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.description: Planning, site evaluation, and District Improvement Financing for wastewater collection and treatment along the Route 9 corridor.
route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.status: Planning for an estimated $40 million to $50 million municipal wastewater system along Route 9 remains under review, with current efforts focused on modular facility design, site identification, and environmental permitting. The Wastewater Study Committee deferred a planned District Improvement Financing warrant article from the fall 2026 Special Town Meeting to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting to allow time for more detailed engineering and financial data. Major hurdles include securing 15 to 20 acres for ground discharge and resolving state Department of Environmental Protection restrictions regarding watershed protection zones.

positions.detail: Supports developing a modular Route 9 collection and treatment system, but postponed bringing financing articles forward until spring 2027 to develop firmer cost estimates.
Voted 4-1 on June 16 to reallocate $30,000 for a District Improvement Financing study, following a 4-0-1 vote in April to extend the wastewater committee's charge through June 2027.

ruby-estates-subdivision.name: Ruby Estates subdivision
ruby-estates-subdivision.description: Six-lot residential subdivision along Lampson Drive off Mount Vickery Road.
ruby-estates-subdivision.status: All six lots in the Ruby Estates subdivision off Mount Vickery Road have been released from covenant following Planning Board approval of a surety agreement in June 2026. Developer Bartolini Builders secured the remaining subdivision improvements with a bond exceeding $324,000 after completing utility installation and the roadway binder course for Lampson Drive. No further municipal board actions are pending.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026, to accept the surety agreement and release all six lots from the subdivision covenant.

rural-cemetery-water-tower.name: Rural Cemetery stone water tower restoration
rural-cemetery-water-tower.description: Proposed structural evaluation, restoration, and Community Preservation Act funding for the historic stone water tower in Rural Cemetery.
rural-cemetery-water-tower.status: The proposed Community Preservation Act application to assess and restore the historic Rural Cemetery stone water tower is deferred to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting to allow time for consultant documentation and bid specifications. The Historical Commission is pursuing funding for structural evaluation, historic standards, and a long-term maintenance plan. Earlier concepts to convert the interior of the tower into a columbarium have been dropped.

positions.detail: Is moving forward with an application for architectural and engineering assessment and restoration bid specifications.
Agreed in August 2026 to defer review of the project to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting cycle.

sarsenstone-way-coc.name: Sarsenstone Way Certificate of Compliance
sarsenstone-way-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review and archival records search for the 1970s Sarsenstone Way subdivision under DEP file 290-100.
sarsenstone-way-coc.status: The Conservation Commission resolved the matter on August 27, 2026, by unanimously approving a full Certificate of Compliance for the Sarsenstone Way subdivision. The decision followed staff locating historic public works as-built plans verifying that all road and drainage requirements were met. With the order closed, no further board action is required.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on August 27, 2026, to issue a full Certificate of Compliance after historic town records verified compliance with subdivision requirements.

scenic-road-tree-removals.name: DPW scenic road tree removals
scenic-road-tree-removals.description: Tree Warden and DPW hearings and approvals to trim or remove public shade trees along designated scenic roads.
scenic-road-tree-removals.status: The Planning Board and Tree Warden approved the DPW's request to remove four trees and trim one tree along designated scenic roads in April 2026 due to decay and safety hazards. During the hearing, questions were raised regarding tree removal priorities near private wells and the status of replacement plantings owed by utility companies. No further hearings or actions are currently scheduled on this application.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on April 27, 2026, to approve the removal of four trees and the trimming of one tree along scenic roads.
Inquiries focused on prioritizing hazard removals along streets reliant on private wells and obtaining owed replacement tree plantings from utilities.

school-bus-transportation-operations.name: School bus transportation and technology
school-bus-transportation-operations.description: Bus operations, safety tracking technologies, and vendor performance oversight with contractor NRT.
school-bus-transportation-operations.status: School bus operations under contractor NRT have stabilized, with turn-by-turn GPS and live security cameras operational across the district fleet. Implementation of student RFID tap cards remains delayed, leading district administration to pursue contractual penalty deductions against the vendor. The Southborough School Committee received an informational update on these operations in May 2026 without taking formal action, and no further public proceedings are currently scheduled.

school-food-service-contract.name: School food service contract renewal
school-food-service-contract.description: Contract administration, financial performance, and annual renewals for district food services with Whitsons Culinary Group.
school-food-service-contract.status: The School Committee has extended the district's food services contract with Whitsons Culinary Group for the 2026–2027 school year. The renewal incorporates a 3.9% CPI adjustment and maintains a guaranteed return provision following an operational deficit of nearly $59,000 largely driven by shifted health insurance costs. School administration is set to review Whitsons' performance in December to determine whether to continue the contract for a third year or put it out to bid.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on May 13, 2026, to extend the contract for the 2026–2027 school year.

school-food-service-contract.next: Administration review of contract performance in December 2026

senior-tax-work-off-policy.name: Senior Tax Work-Off policy and slot allocation
senior-tax-work-off-policy.description: Eligibility regulations and position allocations for Southborough's Senior Tax Work-Off property tax abatement program.
senior-tax-work-off-policy.status: The Senior Tax Work-Off policy is approved and in effect following unanimous Select Board action in September 2026. The latest amendments require CORI background checks for participants and exclude them from other employee benefits, building on an April 2026 update that expanded the program from 30 to 40 positions. No further revisions or board actions are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Sep 2, 2026, to re-approve the policy with CORI check requirements and benefit exclusions, having previously expanded the program to 40 slots.
