southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.name: Southborough Golf Club Audubon management plan
southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.description: Consultant RFP and environmental management plan to achieve Audubon International certification for the Southborough Golf Club.
southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.status: The Golf Committee is moving forward with Audubon International certification for the Southborough Golf Club after approving funding to hire an environmental consultant. With a sole proposal from Conservation Works coming in at $18,400, the committee voted on October 13 to allocate up to $4,500 from its revolving fund to cover the shortfall beyond existing Community Preservation Act funds. Committee members plan to negotiate the final scope and report active progress on environmental stewardship ahead of Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Oct 13 to pay $500 in dues and allocate up to $4,500 from its revolving fund to hire an Audubon certification consultant.
A resident in September asked about total funds allocated and historical efforts regarding building maintenance and Audubon certification.

southborough-golf-club-irrigation.name: Southborough Golf Club irrigation replacement
southborough-golf-club-irrigation.description: Planning, value engineering, and Community Preservation Act funding for replacing the irrigation system at Southborough Golf Club.
southborough-golf-club-irrigation.status: A proposed $1.087 million replacement of the Southborough Golf Club irrigation system heads to Special Town Meeting on October 17 under Article 3. The request seeks $433,546 in new Community Preservation Act funds and $100,000 from the golf revolving fund, while extending $550,000 in previously approved CPA funds. While the Select Board, Community Preservation Committee, and Golf Committee support the article, the Advisory Committee unanimously opposes it, arguing that golf capital improvements should be financed through player fees rather than taxpayer-backed CPA funds. Voters will decide the funding request at Special Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 to recommend approval of Article 3 for Special Town Meeting.
Voted 0-7 against recommending the article, arguing the golf course was meant to be self-sustaining and should fund improvements through player surcharges rather than CPA money.
Voted 4-1 to recommend the warrant article appropriating $433,546 in CPA funds toward the project.
Backs the warrant article as written to complete the project and funded voter outreach ahead of Town Meeting.
Reached consensus supporting the project's preliminary design approach, including stream-safe directional boring and a pump station allowed under the property's conservation restriction.

southborough-golf-club-irrigation.next: Special Town Meeting vote on Article 3 on October 17, 2026

sta-unit-c-contract.name: Southborough Teachers Association Unit C contract
sta-unit-c-contract.description: Three-year collective bargaining agreement between the Southborough School Committee and the Southborough Teachers Association covering Unit C support staff.
sta-unit-c-contract.status: The three-year collective bargaining agreement covering Unit C administrative assistants and educational support professionals has been approved by the Southborough School Committee. District administration described the contract negotiations as collaborative and productive. The finalized document will be made public once ratified by both parties.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 18, 2026, to approve the three-year agreement covering administrative assistants and educational support professionals.

stewardship-committee-structure.name: Stewardship Committee structure and merger proposal
stewardship-committee-structure.description: Deliberation over committee appointments and a proposal to merge the Stewardship Committee with the Open Space Preservation Commission.
stewardship-committee-structure.status: The Select Board resolved an immediate committee vacancy in August 2026 by amending the Southborough Stewardship Committee's charge to create a fourth at-large seat and appointing Freddie Gillespie. However, the board left open the possibility of a broader future review to consolidate town open space and conservation bodies. Both the Stewardship Committee and the Conservation Commission strongly oppose merging Stewardship with the Open Space Preservation Commission, arguing Stewardship must remain independent to focus on land maintenance. No further merger proposals or structural reviews are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 in August to amend the committee charge to an at-large seat and appointed Gillespie 5-0, while discussing broader future reviews of conservation committee roles.
Opposes merging with the Open Space Preservation Commission, arguing it should remain a distinct entity focused strictly on maintaining Breakneck Hill and the Town Forest.
Voted 5-0 on June 25 to send a letter opposing consolidation of Stewardship with Open Space and supporting the preservation of Stewardship's independent mission.
Residents and the Stewardship chair praised Freddie Gillespie's habitat management record and urged the town to preserve experienced volunteer leadership on land management committees.

stormwater-enterprise-fund.name: Stormwater enterprise fund
stormwater-enterprise-fund.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article to establish a municipal enterprise fund for stormwater management accounting and future funding.
stormwater-enterprise-fund.status: Article 5, which would establish a stormwater enterprise fund beginning in fiscal year 2028, is headed to Town Meeting with positive recommendations from both the Select Board and Advisory Committee. The article creates the accounting mechanism only, meaning any future operating budgets or impervious surface user fees would require separate Town Meeting approval. Proponents aim to eventually shift stormwater costs from residential homeowners onto large commercial and tax-exempt parcels.

positions.detail: Voted 7-0 on Sep 16 to recommend Article 5, emphasizing that it establishes the fund structure only and does not implement fees.
Voted 4-1 on Sep 15 to recommend approval of Article 5.

street-tree-planting-program.name: Street tree planting pilot study
street-tree-planting-program.description: A pilot study and planting program to evaluate street canopy cover and identify replacement tree planting locations.
street-tree-planting-program.status: The Planning Board approved a $5,500 pilot study with Davey Resource Group in June 2026 to assess street tree canopy cover and identify replacement planting sites. The study will review 10 to 15 streets starting from the town center to locate approximately 25 viable sites for new trees. A board member was designated to coordinate with the tree warden on long-term planning, and no subsequent public updates have been scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026, to approve spending $5,500 from the tree fund for the pilot study proposal.

town-budget-process-policy.name: Town budget process policy
town-budget-process-policy.description: Draft municipal policy formalizing timelines, board responsibilities, and procedures for constructing the annual town omnibus budget.
town-budget-process-policy.status: The draft policy formalizing timelines and board responsibilities for developing the annual omnibus budget is currently tabled under review. The Select Board halted action to seek guidance from Town Counsel and the Department of Revenue regarding the statutory roles of town administration, the board, and the Advisory Committee. Meanwhile, the Advisory Committee has sought revisions to ensure the policy preserves its independent authority to evaluate, modify, and present the final budget at Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Tabled the draft policy on Sep 15 to consult Town Counsel and state officials regarding statutory versus advisory committee responsibilities.
Drafted revisions to protect its independent statutory authority to recommend and present the budget at Town Meeting, objecting to requirements for a consensus budget.

town-common-fence-restoration.name: Town Common fence restoration
town-common-fence-restoration.description: Repair and restoration of the historic fence and railings at the Town Common funded by the Community Preservation Act.
town-common-fence-restoration.status: The Select Board awarded the base restoration contract to Kneeland Construction to repair and restore the existing Town Common fence using Community Preservation Act funds. Total base project costs are estimated at $82,000 to $83,000, including engineering and construction oversight. The town is seeking funding from MassDOT or planning a separate bid to replace a section of fence lost during a state highway project.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on June 2 to award the base repair bid to Kneeland Construction.

town-forest-footbridge.name: Town Forest Eagle Scout footbridge
town-forest-footbridge.description: Construction materials, permitting, and approvals for an Eagle Scout footbridge project in the Town Forest.
town-forest-footbridge.status: The Stewardship Committee approved the use of pre-cut pressure-treated lumber for the Eagle Scout footbridge project in the Town Forest. The decision resolved questions about whether to substitute cedar near a vernal pool and wetland crossing after reviewing research on minimal copper leaching. No further board reviews or upcoming actions are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Aug 4 to authorize using the pre-cut treated lumber, citing Conservation Commission findings on minimal environmental risk.

town-governance-study.name: Town governance structure study
town-governance-study.description: A consultant-led study evaluating Southborough's municipal government structure, town manager authority, and committee organization.
town-governance-study.status: An 18-week consultant study of Southborough's municipal government structure is currently underway following an initial presentation to the Select Board in early October. The evaluation is examining the town manager's authority, committee organization across Southborough's 68 boards, and potential shifts between charter and bylaw governance models. The Select Board funded the study over dissent regarding town spending ahead of projected budget deficits.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on Aug 11 to authorize the $24,650 consultant contract, with the dissenting member objecting to spending during a tight fiscal environment.

town-satisfaction-survey.name: 2026 Town Satisfaction Survey
town-satisfaction-survey.description: Design, public outreach, and execution of the townwide resident satisfaction survey conducted by the Municipal Technology Committee.
town-satisfaction-survey.status: The 2026 Southborough Satisfaction Survey is currently open to residents and scheduled to run through November 30. The Municipal Technology Committee shortened the survey and condensed question matrices following high drop-off rates in 2025, while adding new sections on affordable housing and senior center services. The Select Board and the Affordable Housing Trust have supported the effort, with the Trust submitting clarifying edits on housing questions prior to launch.

positions.detail: Streamlined question formats to boost completion rates and coordinated townwide outreach to promote participation.
Endorsed the committee's survey prioritization framework on September 2 following a review of the 2025 results.
Submitted revisions on September 23 to simplify question wording and focus options on workforce housing and downtown locations.

town-website-redesign.name: Town website redesign
town-website-redesign.description: Redesign of the municipal website with vendor CivicPlus and consolidation of standalone departmental pages.
town-website-redesign.status: The municipal website redesign is in preparation, with contract and module negotiations with vendor CivicPlus slated to begin in November 2026 and implementation targeted for early 2027. The Municipal Technology Committee has emphasized that successful execution requires dedicated communications support alongside technical staff to manage content and departmental consolidation. IT staff and the committee are reviewing web analytics and regional public engagement data ahead of vendor discussions.

positions.detail: Supports the redesign with CivicPlus but emphasized that the town lacks a communications officer to ensure message consistency during the overhaul.

town-website-redesign.next: Contract and module discussions with CivicPlus in November 2026.

transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.name: Transfer station fees and regulations
transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.description: Department of Public Works updates to transfer station sticker pricing, outside hauling costs, and operational rules for disposal.
transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.status: The Select Board has approved fiscal year 2027 transfer station sticker rates and finalized updated operational regulations, including revised Swap Shop rules. The town also voted to continue participating in a 35-community municipal consortium to negotiate bulk pricing for its next refuse disposal contract ahead of a December 2027 expiration. The board will review and execute Southborough's individual contract terms once consortium negotiations are complete.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Sep 2 to remain in the regional waste disposal consortium, following unanimous approval of updated facility regulations in August.

tricentennial-firefighters-muster.name: 2027 Tricentennial Firefighter's Muster
tricentennial-firefighters-muster.description: Organization of a regional firefighter's muster and antique hand tub demonstration at Woodward School in July 2027.
tricentennial-firefighters-muster.status: Planning is underway for the 2027 antique fire engine muster at the Neary School fields under an approved $25,000 budget. Eight hand tub teams have confirmed participation, and organizers have booked food catering and live music. Site and parking layouts will be presented to the committee in November.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on June 10 to approve a budget up to $25,000 and is reviewing ongoing event preparations.

tricentennial-firefighters-muster.next: Presentation of site and parking layouts at the Tricentennial Committee's November 2026 meeting

tricentennial-first-day.name: First Day 2027 celebration
tricentennial-first-day.description: Planning for Southborough's January 1, 2027 Tricentennial kickoff celebration featuring family activities, a drone show, and a bonfire.
tricentennial-first-day.status: Planning for Southborough's January 1, 2027 Tricentennial kickoff is underway, with a contract executed for a 200-drone aerial light show. The committee is resolving logistics for accompanying activities, replacing a proposed horse-drawn hayride with tractor wagons due to cost and reconsidering the bonfire location due to turf and underground wiring concerns at Woodward School. Organizers are coordinating site walks with town emergency personnel and expect to finalize details at their November meeting.

positions.detail: Contracted Firefly for the New Year's Day drone show while actively refining bonfire, viewing, and transportation logistics.

tricentennial-first-day.next: Site walk to evaluate bonfire locations on October 18, 2026.

tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.name: 2027 Tricentennial Heritage Day Parade
tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.description: Planning for an expanded Heritage Day Parade in October 2027 featuring marching units, community floats, and a historic cannon.
tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.status: Planning is underway for an expanded October 2027 Heritage Day Parade to mark the town's tricentennial. The Tricentennial Committee is currently reviewing logistics, including staging adjustments, spectator turnout strategies, and a proposed Sunday 1:00 PM start to accommodate morning church services. Organizers will next coordinate proposed routes and staging plans with local public safety departments.

positions.detail: Actively planning an expanded 2027 parade, considering adjustments to staging areas, event timing, and additions such as college marching bands and historic artillery.

tricentennial-street-banners.name: Tricentennial commemorative street banners
tricentennial-street-banners.description: Permitting and installation of celebratory banners on utility poles across Southborough's historic villages.
tricentennial-street-banners.status: The Tricentennial Committee is working with town administration to finalize utility permitting and insurance paperwork to hang commemorative street banners for Southborough's 300th anniversary. To avoid utility company inspection fees, the committee directed staff to trim the planned installation to a cap of 50 utility poles. Town staff are continuing coordination with National Grid and Verizon to secure pole attachment permissions.

positions.detail: Supports installing banners across historic villages and directed staff on Oct 14 to cap the list at 50 poles to avoid utility inspection fees.

tricentennial-summer-nights.name: Summer Nights 2027 music festival
tricentennial-summer-nights.description: Expansion of the annual Summer Nights community event into a multi-act music festival for the 2027 Tricentennial.
tricentennial-summer-nights.status: Plans are actively moving forward to expand the annual Summer Nights event into a full-day, multi-stage music festival at the Neary School grounds on August 21, 2027, in celebration of the town's Tricentennial. Organizers are finalizing an agreement with a headliner act to settle audio and stage requirements, and they are reviewing parcel boundaries to explore whether a beer garden could comply with school alcohol prohibitions. Next, the working group will meet with public safety departments, recreation staff, and town administration to review site layout and permitting.

positions.detail: Actively planning the expanded festival, coordinating logistics, and applying for grant funding to support accessibility shuttles and hospitality tents.

tricentennial-summer-nights.next: Filing deadline for accessibility grant application on October 18, 2026.

tricentennial-time-capsule.name: Tricentennial time capsule
tricentennial-time-capsule.description: Selection, preservation, and public placement of a commemorative time capsule for Southborough's 300th anniversary.
tricentennial-time-capsule.status: The Tricentennial Committee is moving forward with plans for a 2-foot cube time capsule to commemorate Southborough's 300th anniversary, selecting indoor storage at the Harvard Depository to preserve materials. Working groups are preparing formal invitations for local civic organizations, clubs, and schools to submit archival-grade photo prints and historical artifacts. Boy Scout Troop 1 has volunteered to assist with community collection efforts.

positions.detail: Supports an archival-standard capsule stored at the Harvard Depository and is issuing submission invitations to local community groups.

trottier-finn-expansion-studies.name: Trottier and Finn expansion feasibility studies
trottier-finn-expansion-studies.description: Proposed Special Town Meeting articles to study expanding Trottier and Finn schools to reconfigure grade levels and take Neary School offline.
trottier-finn-expansion-studies.status: Proposed Special Town Meeting articles seeking up to $500,000 and $324,000 to study expanding Trottier and Finn schools and decommission Neary School face strong municipal opposition. Both the School Committee and the Select Board voted to recommend defeating Articles 2 and 3, citing space analysis showing grade reconfigurations would require sizable building additions to prevent cuts to educational programming. No future meetings or next steps are scheduled in the record.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously to recommend defeating Articles 2 and 3, citing space study findings that grade reconfigurations would require major building additions to prevent severe programming cuts.
Voted 4-1 to recommend that Special Town Meeting defeat Articles 2 and 3.
A resident asked whether the town would have to conduct all three studies if Articles 1, 2, and 3 all pass, and whether study scope covers site capacity for future additions.

trottier-school-roof-replacement.name: Trottier Middle School roof replacement
trottier-school-roof-replacement.description: Proposed funding and MSBA grant reimbursement to replace the roof at Trottier Middle School.
trottier-school-roof-replacement.status: The proposed Trottier Middle School roof replacement is included in the school district's FY27 capital plan, with an estimated gross cost of just under $8.9 million. The project anticipates a Massachusetts School Building Authority grant covering roughly 41% of the total, leaving an estimated net cost to taxpayers of about $5.4 million. Town Meeting voters will be asked to authorize the full gross amount following an anticipated MSBA board decision.

positions.detail: Supports the project as part of the FY27 capital plan and voted 4-0 on March 24, 2026, to approve an informational flyer outlining gross and net costs for voters.

two-family-zoning-amendment.name: Two-family dwelling zoning amendment
two-family-zoning-amendment.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendment for Town Meeting to eliminate the requirement that a single-family dwelling exist for two years before converting to a two-family home.
two-family-zoning-amendment.status: Article 2 is scheduled for the October 17, 2026 Special Town Meeting, proposing to eliminate the two-year waiting period for converting single-family homes into two-family dwellings and permit new two-family construction by special permit. The Zoning Board of Appeals and Select Board recommend approval, while the Advisory Committee recommends against it due to concerns about speculative house-flipping, septic capacity, and neighborhood density. The Planning Board will conclude its public hearing on October 17 immediately before Town Meeting takes up the article.

positions.detail: Sponsored the amendment and voted unanimously on Oct 7 to present the article as drafted to Town Meeting.
Voted 5-0 on Sep 24 to support the revised warrant article.
Voted 3-4 against recommending approval, citing concerns that removing the two-year rule invites speculative flipping and overwhelms septic capacity.
Has not yet taken a position, continuing its public hearing to evaluate potential ambiguities in lot size requirements across zoning districts.
A former Planning Board chair questioned draft phrasing regarding minimum lot sizes, warning it could create loopholes in non-residential districts.

two-family-zoning-amendment.next: Planning Board continued public hearing on October 17, 2026 at 9:05 AM

well-and-septic-regulations.name: Well and septic regulation amendments
well-and-septic-regulations.description: Board of Health regulations governing private well testing, swimming pool setbacks, and subsurface sewage disposal systems.
well-and-septic-regulations.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved amendments to Southborough's private well and septic regulations in July 2026 following a public hearing. The new rules require separation of roles between septic engineers and installers, ensure physical access for septic repairs, establish a 25-foot well setback from swimming pools, and require well testing prior to real estate transfers unless mutually waived. With the revised regulations enacted, no further board action or hearings are scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on July 7, 2026, to approve the updated well and septic regulations.
